description: Build a queue containing the values 1 through n in order. A fetch request selects the current kth value, returns it, and moves it to the back of the queue. Example 1: for n = 8, fetch(3), fetch(5), fetch(2), fetch(8) returns 3, 6, 2, 2. Example 2: for n = 1, fetch(1) always returns 1. Constraints: n and k are positive, and at most 2000 fetch operations are performed.
intuition: Fetching changes the order, so the structure must support both selecting by current rank and appending at the tail.

brute_force.approach: Store values in a list, remove the kth value, and append it.

optimal.approach: Use a Fenwick tree over active positions. Remove the selected rank and insert the value at a fresh tail position.
optimal.space: O(n + q), where q is the number of fetches

edge_cases: Fetching the first or last current item moves that same item to the back.
The append index must keep increasing so old Fenwick positions are never reused.
